steps.say: This archive holds World Bank economic updates on Kenya and Uganda.

steps.speak: It holds no report on Rwanda. A user asks how much Rwanda's economy grew in twenty twenty-five.

steps.say: The search compares the question with every passage in the archive.
It returns the closest passages for every question, including a question from outside the archive.
Here they are a chart of farm output and two passages on growth in East Africa.
The application places these passages in the prompt, together with the instructions and the question.
One line of the instructions asks the model to say so when the passages do not contain what is needed.
The model answers that the passages do not contain Rwanda's growth figure for 2025.

steps.say: The answer cites the only passage in the prompt that mentions Rwanda, a chart with no values in its text.
An application can also stop a question when its closest passage scores below a minimum.
On labelled test questions, the minimum score stops seven questions from outside the archive.
Two others, on growth in Tanzania and on coffee exports from Ethiopia, score above it.
These two questions reach the model, and the instruction on missing answers remains the safeguard.
